text: dawn/stone
Fishers of Men
Jerusalem, around the year 28. You have studied the Law since you could read - lately at the feet of a sharp young Pharisee from Tarsus named Saul.
left
right
There is a carpenter's son preaching by the Sea of Galilee. The crowds call him rabbi. The council wants eyes on him.
Go north with the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law. Watch him. Listen. Bring me back every word - especially the dangerous ones.
I will bring you every word.|What if his words are true?
Good. A sharp ear and a closed heart - that is how the Law is guarded.
(He studies you a long moment) Then the Law will show it. But I doubt the Law has much to fear from Galilee.
dawn/water
Days later you stand on the shore of the lake of Gennesaret. The crowd presses so close around the teacher that he steps into a fishing boat to speak from the water.
center
right
Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.
Master, we worked all night, and caught nothing. (He rubs his tired eyes) But at your word I will let down the net.
The nets fill until they begin to tear. A second boat comes alongside, and both sink low in the water with fish.
(Falling to his knees among the fish) Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord!
Don't be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.
When they had brought their boats to land, they left everything, and followed him.
sunny/stone
That week, in a crowded house in Capernaum, you sit among Pharisees and teachers who have come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem.
Then the roof opens. Four men lower their paralyzed friend on a mat, through the tiles, right down in front of the teacher.
center
Man, your sins are forgiven you.
left
(Under his breath, to you) Who is this that speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

Which is easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Arise and walk'? But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins - arise, take up your cot, and go to your house.
The man stands up in front of them all, takes up his mat, and walks out through the crowd, praising God.

who: What will you write to Saul?
text: Every word, exactly as it happened.|Only that he speaks blasphemy.
You write it all down - the nets, the roof, the forgiveness, the man walking home. Your hand shakes on the last line.
You write one line. You leave out the man walking home, and you cannot say why it feels like a lie.
Amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, 'We have seen strange things today.'

Peter had worked all night and caught nothing. Why do you think he let the nets down anyway?|The Pharisees saw the same miracle as everyone else in the room. What kept them from glorifying God?|Is there something you have been taught to watch with suspicion? What would it take to listen to it honestly?
night/grass
The Sealed Tomb
Two years later. Passover in Jerusalem. The chief priests have put you on the temple guard - and tonight the guard is given torches, clubs, and a guide.
left
Judas will greet the one we want with a kiss. Take him quietly. The city is full of pilgrims who love him.
right
Stay close to me, {hero}. An olive grove at night - a careless guard can lose a foot, or an ear.
In the garden of Gethsemane your torches find a few tired men. One of them walks out to meet you before you can reach him.
right
center
Hail, Rabbi! (He kisses him)
Friend, why are you here?
left
Hands seize him. Then steel flashes in the torchlight - a disciple draws a sword and cuts off the right ear of Malchus, beside you.
Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
He touches Malchus's ear, and it is whole. Malchus stares at you with his hand on his ear, and says nothing at all.
Every one of the disciples flees into the dark. You walk the prisoner back into the city.
storm/stone
On Friday they crucify him outside the city walls. From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covers the whole land. Then the earth shakes.
Truly this was the Son of God.
night/stone
left
The priests remember he said he would rise after three days. Pilate has given us his seal. Nobody touches that stone - not his disciples, not anyone.
Two nights you keep watch at the sealed tomb. On the third, just before dawn, the ground begins to shake beneath your feet.
dawn/stone
center
An angel of the Lord rolls the stone away and sits on it. His appearance is like lightning. You shake, and fall like a dead man.
Through the ringing in your ears you hear him speak - not to you, but to the women who have come with spices.
Don't be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said.
sunny/stone
Some of the guard run to the chief priests. The elders meet, and silver is counted out onto the table in front of you.
right
Say, 'His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.' If the governor hears of it, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble.

who: The silver is in front of you.
text: Take it, and say what you are told.|Leave it on the table.
The coins are heavy and cold. You repeat the words until they almost sound true.
You push the coins back. Caiaphas only smiles - who would believe a guard who slept at his post? You say nothing. Silence is free.
But at night, whenever you close your eyes, you see an empty tomb.
So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.

Jesus healed the ear of a man who came to arrest him. What does that tell you about him?|The guards saw the stone rolled away and still told a different story. Why is it so hard to speak up about something true?|Is there something you know is true, but have kept quiet about?
sunny/stone
The Road to Damascus
A few years on. The followers of the risen Jesus fill Jerusalem - and today one of them, Stephen, has been dragged outside the city to be stoned.
right
Lord Jesus, receive my spirit! (He falls to his knees) Lord, don't hold this sin against them!
left
The witnesses have laid their cloaks at the feet of your teacher, Saul. He watches it all, and approves.
You saw how he died - praying for us. That is how far this poison has spread, {hero}. It has to be cut out.
But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house, and dragged both men and women off to prison.
right
The high priest has given me letters for the synagogues of Damascus. Saddle the horses. Any who belong to the Way, man or woman, we bring back bound.
Ride beside him.|Ride - and keep the tomb to yourself.
Good. There is no one I trust more.
You open your mouth to tell him about the stone, the angel and the silver. Then you close it, and saddle the horses.
sunny/sand
Six days north. Near noon on the last day Damascus rises out of the haze - and on the road ahead, the disciples who fled Jerusalem stand waiting.
dusk/stone
You lead Saul by the hand into Damascus, to the house of Judas on the street called Straight. For three days he neither eats nor drinks. He only prays.
left
right
{hero}... was it like this? The light. At the tomb, all those years ago - did you see a light?
Tell him everything.|Say nothing - not yet.
There was an angel, and the stone was rolled away, and he was not there. I was told to say his disciples stole him. I have known for years, Saul.
(Quietly) Then you knew before I did. And I made you ride with me anyway.
You say nothing. Saul nods slowly in the dark, as if he heard you anyway.
On the third day there is a knock at the door. The man outside is trembling - one of the very disciples you rode north to bind.
center
Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me, that you may receive your sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Something like scales falls from Saul's eyes. He looks first at Ananias, then at you - and he weeps.
(Turning to you) And you, friend. The Lord did not tell me your name. But I think he knew you would be here.
Take it.|Kneel, and ask to be baptized with Saul.
I was at the empty tomb, Ananias. I have been running from it for years. I am done running.
I was at the empty tomb, Ananias. Baptize me too - I am done running.
That day Saul is baptized - and so are you.
Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.

Ananias was afraid of Saul, and went to him anyway. Who might God be asking you to welcome?|Saul's whole life turned around on one road. What changed him - an argument, or meeting Jesus?|Ananias called his enemy 'Brother.' What would it look like to treat someone that way this week?
sunny/cobblestone
The Jailer's Household

Nearly twenty years later. Saul goes by Paul now, and you have walked a thousand miles of road beside him. A vision in the night has brought you all across the sea to Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia.
left
right
By the river a seller of purple cloth named Lydia believes, and opens her house to you. But on the way to prayer, day after day, a slave girl follows you, crying out.
center
These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!
(Turning, grieved) I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!
The spirit leaves her that very hour - and with it, her owners' income. They seize Paul and Silas and drag them into the marketplace before the magistrates.
center
These men, being Jews, are agitating our city, and set forth customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans!
The magistrates order them stripped and beaten with rods, then thrown into the inner prison, their feet fastened in the stocks.
(Hoarse) {hero} - you are not in chains. Go. Tell Luke and Timothy where we are.
left
I once dragged believers off to prison, Silas. I will not walk away from one now.
night/stone
You keep watch by the prison walls as night falls. About midnight, from somewhere deep inside, you hear singing - and then the ground begins to move.
night/stone
The earthquake has thrown every door open and shaken every chain loose. The jailer stands in the wreckage with his sword in his hand.
left
right
Don't harm yourself, for we are all here!
(Falling down, trembling) Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.
That same hour of the night, the jailer washes their wounds. Then he and his whole household are baptized.
left

who: The jailer's hands shake as he washes Silas's back.
text: Help him with the water.|Tell him about the prisons you once filled.
You are kind to a man who beat your friends.
Someone was kind to me once, on the street called Straight.
I locked believers away too, friend. The same Lord who opened these doors opened mine.
(He stares at you) Then there is hope for a man like me.
He brings you all up into his house and sets food before you, and the whole household rejoices.
He brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his household, having believed in God.

Paul and Silas sang hymns in the dark after being beaten. Where does that kind of joy come from?|The prisoners could have run when the doors opened, but stayed. What did that do for the jailer?|Who in your life might be asking, 'What must I do to be saved?' - out loud or not?
dusk/water
The Revelation on Patmos
Around the year 95. Paul and Peter gave their lives in Rome long ago. Your hair is white now, and the road has ended at the sea - on Patmos, a rocky island where Rome sends those it wants forgotten.
left
right
They sent me here for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus. And it seems they sent you for the same, old friend.
We are the last, John - the last who saw him with our own eyes. Who will remember, when we are gone?
On the Lord's day, as John prays on the rocks above the sea, you hear behind you a loud voice, like a trumpet.
night/water
center
Don't be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever.
Write therefore the things which you have seen, and the things which are, and the things which will happen hereafter.
For days John writes: letters to seven churches; a door standing open in heaven; a Lamb who was slain, and lives; and war in heaven, where the dragon is thrown down.
They overcame him because of the Lamb's blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn't love their life, even to death.
left
right
The word of their testimony, {hero}. You were at the tomb that morning. And you have never once written it down.
Write what you saw at the tomb.|Tell it aloud, to everyone on the island.
You write it all: the garden, the seal, the earthquake, the angel, the silver on the table. Sixty years of silence, in a few lines of ink.
That evening, before the prisoners and the guards alike, you tell it all: the garden, the seal, the angel, the silver. You are not afraid.
Then it will be remembered. Now look, {hero} - look at what he showed me at the very end.
dawn/water
center
Behold, I am making all things new.
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.
left
He who testifies these things says, 'Yes, I come quickly.' Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus.

John was exiled for his testimony and still called himself a partner in perseverance. What helps you keep going when faith costs something?|The believers overcame 'by the word of their testimony.' What is your testimony - what has Jesus done in your life?|Revelation ends with all things made new. What do you most long to see made new?
dawn/stone
The Man Nobody Trusted

Three years after the road to Damascus. Saul has escaped the city in a basket let down over the wall, and now the two of you walk back into Jerusalem - the city where he once dragged believers from their houses.
left
right
They will not open their doors to me, {hero}. Why would they? I would not open mine.
He is right. In house after house the disciples hear his name and go pale. A door closes. Then another.
right

(Taking Saul's arm, loud enough for the whole street) Brothers! I have heard this man preach in Damascus with my own ears. He saw the Lord on the road. I will vouch for him - bring him to the apostles.

But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
center
(Studying Saul a long moment) I once swore three times I never knew him. If the Lord can make something of me, he can make something of you. Stay with us, Saul.

who: Peter turns to you. What do you say?
text: I was there at the empty tomb.|I came to arrest you once, too.
(A slow grin) Then you have seen what I have seen. Welcome, {hero}.
(He laughs out loud) So did half this city. Welcome, {hero}.
But the Greek-speaking Jews Saul argues with in the synagogues do not want to argue. They want him dead - and the temple guard has been told which house he sleeps in.
night/stone

Years later the church in Jerusalem is praying through the night at the house of Mary, John Mark's mother. Herod has killed James with the sword and thrown Peter into prison under four squads of soldiers.
left
Keep praying. Mother says we pray until morning, whatever comes.
A knock at the outer gate. The servant girl Rhoda runs to answer it.
right
(Flying back in, breathless) It's Peter! It's Peter's voice at the gate!
Rhoda, you're out of your mind. Peter is in chains.
When she recognized Peter's voice, she didn't open the gate for joy, but ran in, and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.
Peter keeps on knocking. When at last they open the gate, there he stands - an angel has led him out past the guards, through an iron gate that opened by itself.
left
right
Barnabas and Saul are taking the famine gifts back to Antioch. Mark is going with them - and so am I, for a while.
(Already tying up her bundle) Then so am I. Somebody has to answer the door.
But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

Barnabas risked his own good name for a man nobody trusted. Who needs someone to vouch for them near you?|The church prayed all night for Peter - and then didn't believe it when the answer knocked. Why is it so hard to believe our prayers are heard?|Rhoda was so happy she forgot to open the gate. When did good news last make you forget yourself?
sunny/sand
The Centurion's House
Caesarea, the Roman capital on the sea. Statues of Caesar, a harbor of white stone, and soldiers everywhere.
left
I came here after the Ethiopian on the desert road, and never left. My four daughters prophesy - you'll hear them before you see them.
Philip leads you to a house where a Roman centurion is waiting at the door, as if he expected you.
right
I am Cornelius, of the Italian cohort. Some years ago an angel told me to send for a man named Simon Peter. He came, and while he was still speaking the Spirit fell on all of us - Romans, all of us.
I have commanded a hundred men for half my life. Now I would like to serve under someone.
Peter opened his mouth and said, 'Truly I perceive that God doesn't show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.'

who: Cornelius holds out his sword, hilt first. What do you do?
text: Tell him to keep it.|Take it - he won't need it now.
Keep it, Cornelius. Where we're going, someone will need protecting.
(He smiles and hands it over) Then I will carry a walking staff, like the rest of you.

On the next day, we, who were Paul's companions, departed, and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him. Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

Cornelius was a Roman officer - one of the occupiers. What would it have taken for the believers to welcome him?|'God doesn't show favoritism.' Who are you tempted to think God favors less?|Philip stayed and served in one city for years. Is God asking you to go, or to stay?
sunny/grass
First Called Christians

Antioch on the Orontes, the third city of the empire. Here, for the first time, Greeks who have never kept the Law are believing in great numbers - and Barnabas has fetched Saul from Tarsus to teach them.
left
right
In the market they've started calling us 'Christ-people' - Christianoi. I don't think they mean it kindly.
(Laughing) Let them. It's a better name than most of us deserve.
When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
Some men down from Judea say I'm not really one of you - not until I keep the whole Law. Am I one of you, {hero}?
You were one of us the day you believed.|Come to Jerusalem and let the apostles say it.
(Letting out a long breath) Then I'm coming with you. Wherever the road goes.
Then I'll go to Jerusalem and stand in front of them myself. Wherever the road goes, I'm on it.
But not everyone in Antioch welcomes a new kind of people. Word comes that a cohort has been sent to break up the gathering.
dusk/grass
The council in Jerusalem has spoken: the Gentiles are not to be burdened with the whole Law. Two men have carried the letter back to Antioch, and the church reads it aloud with joy.
right
Judas Barsabbas goes home tomorrow. I am staying. The letter says the Gentiles are free - I would like to see it with my own eyes, city by city.
left
Barnabas and I have parted ways over Mark. It grieves me. Will you come with me, Silas?
(Picking up his staff) I thought you'd never ask.
but Paul chose Silas, and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God.

The believers in Antioch were given a name by outsiders. What would people around you call you, by what they see?|The church settled a fierce argument by listening, Scripture and prayer. How do you handle disagreements about faith?|Paul and Barnabas split over Mark - and years later Paul called Mark useful. Is there a broken friendship you could still mend?
sunny/dirt
A Donkey Named Barley
Lystra, a little town in the hills of Lycaonia. The last time Paul came here, he healed a man lame from birth - and the crowd decided he and Barnabas were Zeus and Hermes come down.
left
They brought oxen and garlands to the city gate to sacrifice to us. Barnabas tore his clothes. I shouted myself hoarse.

Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky and the earth and the sea, and all that is in them;
Then men came from Antioch and Iconium, and the same crowd stoned me and dragged me out of the city for dead. Still - some believed.
left
right
Some believed. I am one, and my daughter Eunice is another - and her son Timothy is the third, though he is shy about saying so.
We taught him the Scriptures since he was small enough to sit on my knee. Paul, take him with you. And take us too - someone has to feed you all.
center
Mother! (Then, quietly, to Paul) ...I would like to come. If you'll have me.
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you; which lived first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice, and, I am persuaded, in you also.

As you leave the gate, something nudges you hard in the back. A small grey donkey stands there, still wearing a wilted garland from the sacrifice that never happened, with two saddlebags of Eunice's bread on her back.
center
(Hee-haw!)
Oh - that's Barley. She carried the garlands that day, and she has followed Paul around the town ever since. She won't go home. I've tried.

who: Barley stamps one hoof. What do you do?
text: Let her come.|Try to send her home.
A donkey carried our Lord into Jerusalem. I suppose one can carry our bread.
You point firmly back toward the town. Barley looks at you, sits down in the middle of the road, and does not move until you give up. She's coming.
Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, 'What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?'

The crowd at Lystra praised Paul one day and stoned him soon after. Why did he go back?|Timothy's faith 'lived first' in his grandmother and mother. Whose faith lived in someone before it reached you?|Even a stubborn donkey has a place in this story. What small or stubborn thing might God use in you?
night/wood
The Boy in the Window
Troas, a port on the edge of Asia. Every road forward has closed - and then, in the night, Paul sees a man of Macedonia standing and begging, 'Come over and help us.'
left
I am a physician. I have treated sailors from every port on this coast. You'll want a doctor where you're going - and someone to write it all down, carefully, from the beginning.

A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him, and saying, 'Come over into Macedonia and help us.' When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.
Years later you pass through Troas again. On the first day of the week the church gathers in an upper room to break bread, and Paul, leaving in the morning, talks... and talks... until midnight.
A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, sinks into a deep sleep - and falls three stories to the ground.
right
(Kneeling in the street) He is dead. I am sorry - there is nothing -
left
(Throwing himself down and wrapping his arms around the boy) Don't be troubled. His life is in him.
Paul goes back upstairs, breaks the bread, and talks until dawn. Eutychus, very much alive, sits right at the front this time - and asks to come along.
center
I'll stay awake for the next one. Probably.
They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

Paul found the way forward only after other doors closed. Has a closed door ever led you somewhere better?|Luke was a careful writer who checked everything. Why does it matter that the gospel was written down carefully?|Eutychus fell asleep in church - and was raised anyway. What does that tell you about God's patience with us?
sunny/sand
Tentmakers and a Letter-Carrier
Corinth, a city of two harbors, rich and rough and proud of both. Paul arrives tired and nearly penniless, and goes looking for work with his hands.
left
right
Claudius threw every Jew out of Rome, so here we are, stitching tents in Corinth. You know the trade? Then pull up a stool.
And stay with us. We have a room, and you look like you haven't slept in a bed since Athens.
Because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.
By day, canvas and leather. On the Sabbath, the synagogue. Many believe - and many others are furious. A crowd gathers at the workshop door.
(Setting down her awl) Well. It seems the tents will have to wait.
dusk/water
The Lord has spoken to Paul in a vision: 'Don't be afraid, but speak and don't be silent; for I am with you.' He stays a year and a half.
In Cenchreae, Corinth's eastern port, the church meets in the house of a woman named Phoebe. She has helped so many travelers that half the harbor owes her a favor.
right
I have business in Rome, Paul. If you have a letter for the believers there, I will carry it myself - and see it read aloud.
left
(Smiling) Then the letter had better say something about you.

I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae, that you receive her in the Lord, in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.

Paul worked a trade alongside his preaching. How can ordinary work be part of serving God?|Priscilla and Aquila opened their home and later 'risked their own necks' for Paul. What does hospitality cost?|Phoebe was trusted to carry the most important letter Paul ever wrote. Who has God trusted you to carry something to?
sunny/cobblestone
Great Is Artemis!
Ephesus: marble streets, a theater for twenty-five thousand, and the great temple of Artemis, one of the wonders of the world. Half the city earns its bread from her pilgrims.
left
right
I have preached in the synagogue for weeks. They tell me I speak like Moses himself. And yet you two keep looking at me as if I'd left out a chapter.
(Kindly) Come to supper, Apollos. Aquila and I will tell you the rest of it.
Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.
(Days later) The rest of it is better than anything I was saying. I will not keep quiet now.
Two years on, so many have turned from the idols that the silversmiths who make little silver shrines of Artemis are going hungry. One of them, Demetrius, calls a meeting.
center
This Paul says that gods made with hands are no gods at all! Our trade is ruined - and the temple of the great goddess will count for nothing!
The crowd pours into the theater, shouting. Most of them do not even know why they are there.
dusk/stone
For two hours the theater roars, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' - until the town clerk finally quiets them and sends them home.
left
I am going on to Corinth. They need someone to water what Paul planted.
right
I planted, Apollos watered - but God gives the growth. Go with my blessing.
But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!'

Apollos was gifted and sincere, and still needed teaching. Who has helped you understand faith 'more accurately'?|The silversmiths cared most about their trade. What do people around you protect, even against the truth?|Most of the crowd didn't know why they were shouting. When have you gone along with a crowd?
